title: Create Notes on the Board
lede: The first feature, and the foundation for the rest: a pointer event becomes a rect in pure geometry, a command turns it into an action, a pure reducer commits it, and only the components that selected what changed render again.

steps.title: The stores are created, then React renders
steps.explain: Two stores are made **before** the first render and passed in, not imported. That is why every test can mount the same App on fresh stores. Rendering still comes before the network.

steps.title: App connects the top bar to the scroll container
steps.explain: The toolbar is a sibling of the Board but must know which part of it is visible, so App owns one ref and passes it to both. A ref changing causes no render, and the Context value never changes either.

steps.title: The Board starts listening for presses
steps.explain: After mounting, the Board listens on the **document**, because a double-click can start on the top bar or the backdrop. The cleanup removes that listener. Without it, StrictMode's second run in development would leave two, and each press would fill both slots of the window. Removing it was tried, and double-clicks starting on a Note created again.

steps.title: The hint shows
steps.explain: `EmptyHint` selects a boolean, so it renders again only when the Board becomes empty or stops being empty. It sits outside the scrolling content, so it stays centred without a scroll listener. Its CSS has `pointer-events: none`, so double-clicking the hint reaches the Board.

steps.title: Each press records where it landed
steps.explain: `dblclick` reports only the second press, so the Board keeps the last two on the page: each press moves `last` into `previousToLast`. The **capture** phase means it still hears a press if a Note stops propagation, which a script checked in both browsers. No test covers it.

steps.title: The double-click becomes a Board point
steps.explain: Both presses were on empty Board, so it continues. `getBoundingClientRect()` already includes scrolling, so one subtraction is enough. In a 1024×768 window, a double-click at client (260, 250) is Board (260, 202): the top bar is 48 px.

steps.title: The point becomes a rect
steps.explain: The default size is Medium, 220×170, so that Note lands at (150, 117). Rounding comes **before** clamping: the bounds are whole pixels, and rounding a width up afterwards could push the right edge to 1921.

steps.title: The command adds the Current colour
steps.explain: The colour lives in the UI store and the Note in the Notes store. Neither reducer knows the other, so this rule lives in a command. The id is also made here, which keeps the reducer pure.

steps.title: The reducer commits it
steps.explain: It clamps again, because it can't trust every caller. The Note gets `z = topZ + 1`. The other Notes keep their references. The store tells subscribers only because the state object changed.

steps.title: Only the Board and the new Note render
steps.explain: The Board selects `ids`, which changed. Each Note selects itself and is memoised, so the others skip. This was measured with temporary render counters in both browsers: a create rendered the Board and the new Note, and a change to one Note rendered only that Note. The automated Profiler test arrives with #4.

steps.title: A double-click on a Note
steps.explain: Both presses report a target inside a Note, not the Board itself, so the handler returns before any maths.

steps.title: A double-click that only starts on a Note
steps.explain: A press just inside a Note's edge, then one just outside, is a `dblclick` on the Board. Checking only that event's target created an overlapping Note in both browsers. Review found it, and this test failed before the fix.

steps.title: A double-click that starts outside the Board
steps.explain: A press on the top bar or backdrop, then one on empty Board, is also a `dblclick` on the Board. The outside press is recorded as `false`, so nothing is created. When only the Board listened, that press went unseen and an older press took its place. The test makes that older press first, and it failed in both browsers before the fix.

steps.title: An action that changes nothing
steps.explain: A `load` of equal Notes returns the **same** state, so the store notifies nobody and nothing renders. Equal Notes also keep their references, which the later `diffNotes` needs, or a load would look like a round of edits.

steps.title: The visible area is read on press
steps.explain: `clientWidth` and `clientHeight` leave out scrollbars, where `offsetWidth` would not. The Notes are read with `getSnapshot()`, not subscribed to, so the toolbar doesn't render on every change.

steps.title: The centre ignores the backdrop
steps.explain: A 2560 px wide window shows only 1920 px of Board, so the centre is 960, not 1280. In the real build at 2560×1400, M landed at (850, 455).

steps.title: A second press cascades
steps.explain: While a Note has that exact top-left, the spot steps by (24, 24). At one edge it keeps stepping along the other axis.

steps.title: The cascade wraps from the corner
steps.explain: In the bottom-right corner a step clamps back to the same spot, so the cascade restarts at the top-left of the **visible** Board. The Board's own top-left could be off-screen. Each wrap starts 24 px further right, or every wrap would repeat one diagonal. In the production build at 1024×768, scrolled to the end, 100 presses of each size gave 100 distinct Notes, all in view, in both browsers.

steps.title: Every spot is taken
steps.explain: When a wrap would start past the last x that fits, it stops, and only then do Notes stack. Without the `break` this would loop forever and freeze the tab. Scrolled to the end at 1024×768, a script found 545 distinct Medium spots before that happens.

steps.title: Coordinates, by example and by property
steps.explain: The examples use literal numbers. The properties try random rects: inside the Board, never under 140×100, and clamping twice equals clamping once. The cascade test presses 100 times: it got 51 distinct spots before each wrap moved right.

steps.title: References, not just values
steps.explain: `toBe` checks identity. A reducer that copied every Note would pass `toEqual` and fail here.

steps.title: The Current colour
steps.explain: The store starts at blue, because a hard-coded yellow would pass with the default. Hard-coding it was tried, and this test failed.

steps.title: What must not compile
steps.explain: A plain string is not a `NoteId`, red is not a `NoteColour`, and an unknown action is not a `NoteAction`. Widening the first two types to `string` was tried, and their tests failed.

steps.title: A real mouse in two browsers
steps.explain: Headless scrollbars take no space, so borders stand in for them. Swapping `clientWidth` for `offsetWidth` was tried, and all three size tests failed in both browsers.

notes.title: Presses are recorded on the document.
notes.detail: Explaining `rememberPress` exposed the bug: the Board heard only its own presses, so an old one could pair with a double-click that started outside it. The counter-argument is that a component now has a page-wide listener, where a React prop was simpler. It does one comparison per press and is removed on unmount. A press outside the page itself is still invisible to it.

notes.title: The cascade wraps from the corner.
notes.detail: The spec doesn't say what happens there, so the owner chose wrapping, for user story 11: "don't hide exactly on top". Stopping was one line and more predictable. The cost of wrapping is a jump back across the screen and a search that grows with the Notes: the slowest placement measured was 20 ms, with about 2,300 Notes.

notes.title: The cascade can leave the visible area before it wraps.
notes.detail: It follows the spec's (24, 24) steps to the Board's corner, not the window's. At 1024×768 scrolled to the top-left, 6 of 25 presses of M made Notes wholly out of view. This is open for the owner: wrapping at the visible edge would fix it.

notes.title: `user-select: none` is always on the Board.
notes.detail: The spec says "during a Gesture". Double-click is a command here, and would otherwise select text. #7 has to set `user-select: text` on the textarea.

notes.title: `touch-action: none` waits for #4.
notes.detail: It belongs with Gestures. Added now, it would remove touch scrolling of the Board and give nothing back.

notes.title: App, not the Board, owns the scroll container ref.
notes.detail: The top bar is outside the Board and needs it. The owner agreed that #6's `BoardDomContext` is provided by App, and #6 now says so. The spec in #1 still says the Board.

notes.title: The scroll container has a 24 px gutter at the right and bottom.
notes.detail: Without it, the Board's edge is off-screen when scrolled to the end. There is none at the top-left, so scroll offsets are still Board coordinates. The left edge line is inset for the same reason.

notes.title: `StoresContext` has no `sync` yet, and the UI store has no actions.
notes.detail: `sync` arrives with saving (#10). Each UI action arrives with its feature. Until then `UiAction` is `never`, so dispatching anything fails to compile.

notes.title: Only yellow is styled.
notes.detail: It is the only colour a user can create before #8, which adds the other five and the glyphs on the buttons.

notes.title: A reload loses the Notes.
notes.detail: Nothing is saved until #9. The startup GET is still only logged.

notes.title: fast-check is pinned to 4.10.2.
notes.detail: 4.11.0 was published hours before this change. An older release is the more cautious dev dependency.
